note: From the Town of Conway's own pages (departments, Documents, Public Notices, town code), the Conway Forward zoning project site, the Mt Washington Valley Chamber of Commerce, NH state agencies and open Conway Daily Sun coverage. North Conway is a village in the Town of Conway, so permits and licenses run through Conway Town Hall at 23 Main Street in Conway Village.

organizations.name: Mt Washington Valley Chamber of Commerce
organizations.what: Chamber at 2473 White Mountain Highway, North Conway, with close to 600 member businesses and organizations that support growth and promote the Mt. Washington Valley as a place to live, work and visit.

source.label: Mt Washington Valley Chamber of Commerce

organizations.name: Mt Washington Valley Economic Council
organizations.what: Nonprofit founded in 1990 that runs a Revolving Loan Fund for local businesses (it lent $560,000 to 27 small businesses during the pandemic). In June 2026 it sold its Technology Village office space to Northeast Woodland Chartered Public School, planned to leave by August 1 and was discussing a possible merger with a larger economic council. Executive director Jac Cuddy. Phone and website from its Chamber directory listing.

organizations.name: NH Small Business Development Center, North and Central Region
organizations.what: Business advising; the regional office is at the Grafton Regional Development Council, 131 Main Street, Plymouth. The SBDC locations page does not list which towns each office serves; request advising through nhsbdc.org.

organizations.name: NH DHHS Food Protection Section
organizations.what: State office that licenses anyone who makes, stores or sells food in New Hampshire (except in self-inspecting communities) and reviews floor plans for new or remodeled food businesses.

organizations.name: Congressman Chris Pappas, North Conway office
organizations.what: District office at 2541 White Mountain Highway, Building 1 Unit 4, North Conway, for help with federal agencies; the office does not receive mail.

cityOffices.name: Planning and Zoning (Town Hall, 23 Main St, Conway)
cityOffices.what: Staffs the Planning Board and Zoning Board of Adjustment and reviews site plan and subdivision applications. Director of Planning and Development Ryan O'Connor, Planner Holly Whitelaw, Zoning Administrator Bill Barbin. Zoning permit, site plan, temporary event permit and ZBA forms are on the town Documents page. The Kearsarge Lighting Precinct has its own zoning, which the town does not enforce.

source.label: Town of Conway, Planning and Zoning

cityOffices.name: Building Inspection and Code Enforcement
cityOffices.what: Building permits (apply online through Cloudpermit) and building, fire, health and zoning inspections; helps new and existing businesses with moves and expansions. Building Inspector Jeremy Gibbs. Codes include the 2021 IBC, 2021 IRC and 2021 NFPA 101 Life Safety Code.

source.label: Town of Conway, Building Inspection and Code Enforcement

cityOffices.name: Town Clerk and Tax Collector
cityOffices.what: Vehicle and boat registrations, vital records and property tax payments; also sells summer recreation parking stickers. Town Clerk/Tax Collector Louise Inkell. Closed daily 12:30 to 1:30 p.m.

source.label: Town of Conway, Town Clerk and Tax Collector

cityOffices.name: Assessing
cityOffices.what: Property values, abatement and exemption forms, and owner, location or map-and-parcel reports (spreadsheets by email for $100). Online tax maps and cards through AxisGIS. Chief Assessor Thomas Hughes.

cityOffices.name: Town Manager's office
cityOffices.what: Handles recreation parking passes for business-owned vehicles and extra passes for trusts and LLCs (by application, not in person).

howTo.title: Open a business in a commercial space
howTo.steps: Check zoning with Planning and Zoning (603-447-3811, ext. 223); a change or expansion of use may need Planning Board site plan review and a zoning permit (forms on the town Documents page). Every commercial improvement needs a building permit, whatever the cost, and the building inspector may require a certificate of occupancy for a commercial remodel or a change in tenancy. Commercial applications need architectural or structural documents. Apply for building permits online through Cloudpermit. Contractors must register with the town (no fee).

source.label: Town of Conway Code, Chapter 23 Building Construction

howTo.title: Put up a sign
howTo.steps: Signs need a town sign permit. The Sign Permit form is posted under both Building and Public Works and Planning and Zoning on the town Documents page; call Planning and Zoning (603-447-3811, ext. 223) with questions about sign rules for your district.

howTo.title: Run a short-term rental
howTo.steps: In 2023 the NH Supreme Court (Town of Conway v. Kudrick) held that Conway's zoning ordinance allows non-owner-occupied short-term rentals in residential districts. The town runs a Rental Certificate Program: owners of one- and two-family rentals file a self-affidavit, multi-family owners register, and a rental inspection fee schedule applies (all on the town Documents page). The town's zoning rewrite (Conway Forward) is underway, with Planning Board hearings in November and December 2026, so check with Planning and Zoning before you buy or list.

source.label: Town of Conway, Documents (Rental Certificate Program)

howTo.title: Get a food license (restaurant, cafe, food truck, food maker)
howTo.steps: Food licenses come from the state, not the town: apply to the NH DHHS Food Protection Section with the fee. For a newly built or remodeled kitchen, submit a Floor Plan Review Application (online portal with a Food Operation Questionnaire, or on paper) before licensing. Questions: 603-271-4589. Building and fire code work still goes through Conway's Building Inspection office.

source.label: NH DHHS, Submit a Floor Plan Review

howTo.title: Hold a special or temporary event
howTo.steps: Use the town's Special Event Permit application and guidelines, or the Planning and Zoning Temporary Event Permit, both on the Documents page. Events in Schouler Park need a special events permit approved by the Board of Selectmen; athletic events in town parks need a memorandum of agreement. Raffles need a town raffle permit.

howTo.title: Plan for winter parking and snow
howTo.steps: From November 15 to April 15 there is no parking on town streets from midnight to 8 a.m. (1:15 a.m. start in some liquor-license areas), and businesses may not push snow or ice onto streets or sidewalks. Fines are $100 for a first offense and $500 after that.

notices.title: Conway Forward zoning rewrite: Planning Board hearings Nov 5 and Dec 3
notices.detail: The town is rewriting its zoning ordinance and map to match the 2024 Conway Forward Master Plan (consultant Barrett Planning Group). The second community meeting was October 22; the October 2026 draft ordinance and table of uses are posted. Planning Board public hearings are November 5 and December 3, 2026 (January 7, 2027 if needed), 6:30 p.m., before a 2027 Town Meeting vote.
